items.title: Default OAuth apps for external AI agents are now generally available
items.excerpt: ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code, and Cursor can now connect to Azure Databricks MCP servers, including the Genie One MCP server, using default OAuth client IDs. An account admin doesn't need to create an OAuth app. See Default OAuth client IDs .

items.title: AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions is now generally available
items.excerpt: AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions is now generally available . Metastore admins can use Unity Catalog permissions on the system.ai schema to control which task-specific AI Functions users in your organization can run. Contact your Databricks account team to enable this feature. See AI Functions Unity Catalog permissions .

items.title: Improved Lakeflow Performance Observability will soon be available by default for workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled
items.excerpt: Starting on or after November 25, 2026, Improved Lakeflow Performance Observability will be available by default for eligible workspaces with the compliance security profile enabled. Lakeflow Jobs now show query performance metrics and insights at the job level for supported tasks. You can view job-level data volume metrics and use the Optimize button to open Genie Code to help improve queries with performance insights. Query profiling is supported for serverless compute, SQL Warehouses and Lakeflow Pipelines. See View query performance metrics for serverless jobs .

Discovery filters disabled modules before importlib.import_module is called, so the default opt-in-off state incurs no import cost. items.title: Databricks ADBC connector for Power BI and Microsoft Fabric (Generally Available)
items.excerpt: This release is part of the broader ODBC-to-ADBC transition for Power Query connectors described in the Transition from ODBC to ADBC drivers in Power BI and Microsoft Fabric documentation. What’s new Existing connections in your semantic models, dataflows, and paginated reports continue to work unchanged — the migration path is currently opt-in per connection, per workspace, or per tenant. Highlights: Improved security - ADBC drivers incorporate security enhancements, such as memory safety and garbage collection. No changes to existing behavior - This transition moves away from the embedded ODBC drivers that ship with Power BI. It does not change behavior for the ODBC connector when you use a separately installed ODBC driver. Efficient large dataset support - ADBC provides a set of standard interfaces for interacting with Arrow data, which is especially efficient at fetching large datasets with minimal overhead and no serialization or copying. Supported authentication - Databricks ADBC supports OAuth (user), OAuth (M2M / Client Credentials), and Microsoft Entra ID. items.title: Modern Power BI architecture choices for reporting on Azure Databricks: A performance benchmark for Power BI storage modes
items.excerpt: Many enterprise Power BI semantic models use Azure Databricks as a data source. When building these models, developers and architects face an early and consequential decision: which storage mode to use. Cost, security, and ease of development and tuning all factor in — but report performance is probably the most important of them, because reports that are slow to load are one of the most common causes of end-user dissatisfaction. In practice, that decision is often made on intuition rather than evidence. To help change that, we've published a new white paper, Modern Power BI Architecture Choices for Reporting on Azure Databricks , benchmarking four ways of serving the same Delta tables to a Power BI report: Direct Lake on OneLake — over Delta tables in a Fabric lakehouse or warehouse Direct Lake on mirrored Unity Catalog tables — shortcuts, no copy DirectQuery — on a Databricks SQL warehouse Composite Model on Databricks — DirectQuery combined with Import-mode aggregations Figure: The four Power BI storage modes benchmarked to evaluate their impact on report performance and scalability. items.title: QuickBooks connector is available in Beta
items.excerpt: The managed QuickBooks connector is now available in Beta in Databricks Lakeflow Connect. Use the connector to ingest accounting data such as accounts, customers, vendors, items, invoices, bills, payments, and journal entries from QuickBooks Online into Azure Databricks. The connector uses OAuth user authorization and supports incremental ingestion with delete capture.
